eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Diabetes diagnosis and insulin therapy
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have had a diagnosis of either: [1a] T1DM based on the World Health Organization (WHO) diagnostic criteria, and have been on the following daily insulin therapy for at least 1 year: [A] multiple daily injection of long-acting insulin analog (either insulin glargine [U-100 or U-300] or insulin degludec [U-100]) and rapid-acting insulin analog (insulin lispro, insulin aspart, or insulin glulisine), or [B] continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII); Or [1b] T2DM based on the WHO diagnostic criteria, and have received the following daily insulin therapy with or without oral anti-hyperglycemic medications (OAMs) for at least 1 year: [A] insulin: long-acting insulin analog (either insulin glargine [U-100 or U-300] or insulin degludec [U-100]) alone, or in combination with rapid-acting insulin analog (insulin lispro, insulin aspart, or insulin glulisine) or CSII; [B] OAM: up to 3 of the following OAMs in accordance with local regulations: metformin, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor, sodium glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, sulfonylurea (should not be more than half of maximum approved doses), glinides, alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, or thiazolidine

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Male contraception agreement
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: male patients: agree to use an effective method of contraception for the duration of the study and for 28 days following the last study treatment

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Female contraception and pregnancy requirements
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: female patients: [3a] women of childbearing potential who are abstinent (if this is complete abstinence, as their preferred and usual lifestyle) or in a same sex relationship (as part of their preferred and usual lifestyle) must agree to either remain abstinent or stay in a same sex relationship without sexual relationships with males. Periodic abstinence (eg, calendar, ovulation, symptothermal, post-ovulation methods), declaration of abstinence just for the duration of a trial, and withdrawal are not acceptable methods of contraception. [3b] otherwise, women of childbearing potential participating must agree to use one highly effective method (less than 1% failure rate) of contraception, or a combination of 2 effective methods of contraception for the entirety of the study. [A] women of childbearing potential participating must test negative for pregnancy prior to initiation of treatment as indicated by a negative serum pregnancy test at the screening visit followed by a negative urine pregnancy test within 24 hours prior to exposure. [B] either one highly effective method of contraception or a combination of 2 effective methods of contraception will be used. The patient may choose to use a double barrier method of contraception. Barrier protection methods without concomitant use of a spermicide are not a reliable or acceptable method. Thus, each barrier method must include use of a spermicide. It should be noted that the use of male and female condoms as a double barrier method is not considered acceptable due to the high failure rate when these methods are combined. [3c] women not of childbearing potential may participate, and include those who are: [A] infertile due to surgical sterilization (hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, or tubal ligation), congenital anomaly such as mullerian agenesis; Or [B] postmenopausal, defined as either: [i] a woman at least 50 years of age with an intact uterus, not on hormone therapy, who has had either: [a] cessation of menses for at least 1 year, or [b] at least 6 months of spontaneous amenorrhea with a follicle-stimulating hormone >40 mIU/mL; or [ii] a woman 55 or older not on hormone therapy, who has had at least 6 months of spontaneous amenorrhea, or [iii] a woman at least 55 years of age with a diagnosis of menopause prior to starting hormone replacement therapy

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Age range
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are between 18 and 64 years old for T1DM, or between 20 and 70 years old for T2DM at the time of informed consent

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Body mass index
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a body mass index of 18.5 to 30.0 kg/m2 for T1DM, or 18.5 to 35.0 kg/m2 for T2DM at the time of screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Hemoglobin A1c value
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a hemoglobin A1c value ≤10% at the time of screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Clinical laboratory test results
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have clinical laboratory test results within normal reference range (except for glycemic parameters) for the population or investigative site, or results with acceptable deviations that are judged to be not clinically significant by the investigator

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Venous access
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have venous access sufficient to allow for blood sampling and administration of insulin for IV administration as per the protocol

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Reliability and availability
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are reliable and willing to make themselves available for the duration of the study and are willing to follow study procedures

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Informed consent
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are able and willing to give signed informed consent

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Investigative site personnel exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are investigative site personnel directly affiliated with this study and their immediate families. Immediate family is defined as a spouse, biological or legal guardian, child, or sibling

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Lilly employees exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are Lilly employees

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Current enrollment in another clinical trial
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are currently enrolled in a clinical trial involving an investigational product or any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Recent participation in clinical trial with investigational product
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have participated, within the last 4 months, in a clinical trial involving an investigational product. If the previous investigational product has a long half-life, 4 months or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) should have passed from the last dose of investigational product

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Prior LY900018 study participation
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have previously completed or withdrawn from this study or any other study investigating LY900018, and have previously received LY900018

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Known allergies to LY900018 or glucagon
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have known allergies or sensitivity to LY900018, glucagon, related compounds, or any components of the formulation, or history of significant atopy

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Abnormal ECG
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have an abnormality in the 12-lead ECG that, in the opinion of the investigator, increases the risks associated with participating in the study

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Significant changes in insulin regimen or unstable blood glucose control
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: any significant changes in insulin regimen and/or unstable blood glucose control within the past 3 months prior to screening as assessed by the investigator

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: High total daily dose of insulin
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have received a total daily dose of insulin >1.2 U/kg at the time of screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Poorly controlled hypertension
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have poorly controlled hypertension (ie, supine systolic BP >165 mm Hg or supine diastolic BP >95 mm Hg) at screening, or a change in antihypertensive medications within 30 days prior to screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: History of pheochromocytoma or insulinoma
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history of pheochromocytoma (ie, adrenal gland tumor) or insulinoma

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: History of severe hypoglycemia or loss of consciousness
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history of an episode of severe hypoglycemia (as defined by an episode that required third party assistance for treatment) in the 1 month prior to screening or have a history of loss of consciousness within the last 2 years induced other than by hypoglycemia

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: History of epilepsy or seizure disorder
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history of epilepsy or seizure disorder

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: History or presence of significant organ disorders
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history or presence of cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine (apart from T1DM or T2DM), hematological, or neurological disorders capable of significantly altering the absorption, metabolism, or elimination of drugs; of constituting a risk when taking the investigational product; or of interfering with the interpretation of data

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Known or ongoing psychiatric disorders
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have known or ongoing psychiatric disorders that, in the opinion of the investigator, may preclude the patient from following and completing the protocol

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Drug abuse
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: regularly use known drugs of abuse and/or show positive findings on urinary drug screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: HIV infection
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection and/or positive HIV antibodies and/or antigen

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Hepatitis C
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of hepatitis C and/or positive hepatitis C antibody

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Hepatitis B
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of hepatitis B and/or positive hepatitis B surface antigen

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Syphilis
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of syphilis and/or are positive for syphilis test

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Lactating women
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are women who are lactating

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Use of prohibited medications
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: use of daily systemic beta-blocker, indomethacin, warfarin, anticholinergic drugs

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Blood donation
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have donated 400 mL or more blood in the last 12 weeks (males) or in the last 16 weeks (females), or any blood donation (including apheresis) within the last 4 weeks, or total volume of blood donation within 12 months is 1200 mL (males)/800 mL (females) or more at screening

arms.name: LY900018 (Nasal Glucagon)
arms.description: Single 3-mg dose of nasal glucagon (LY900018) administered intranasally by study site personnel during one of the two crossover periods

arms.name: IMG (Intramuscular Glucagon)
arms.description: Single 1-mg dose of intramuscular glucagon (GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered by IM injection by study site personnel during one of the two crossover periods

objectives.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
objectives.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non-inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin-induced hypoglycemia using a non-inferiority margin of 10%

endpoints.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint
endpoints.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

objectives.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
objectives.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

endpoints.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Endpoint
endpoints.text: SAE, TEAEs (including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal AEs), vital signs

objectives.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
objectives.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

endpoints.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Endpoint
endpoints.text: PK parameters include AUC, Cmax, Tmax

objectives.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
objectives.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

endpoints.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Endpoint
endpoints.text: PD parameters include BGmax and Tmax

estimands.name: Primary Efficacy Estimand - Non-inferiority of Nasal Glucagon vs Intramuscular Glucagon
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) or type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) who undergo controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia, meeting all eligibility criteria (Intent-to-Treat (ITT) Population - all randomized patients completing both periods with evaluable primary outcome (at least 66 patients, including at least 30 T1DM and 30 T2DM)) Summary measure: Difference in proportions (percentage of patients achieving treatment success: IMG minus LY900018) with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of both periods
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues from the study before completing both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason (e.g., withdrawal of consent, adverse event, protocol deviation)

intercurrentEvents.name: Administration of additional treatments to increase plasma glucose
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives additional treatments to increase plasma glucose within 30 minutes after glucagon administration, which is incorporated directly into the definition of treatment failure (i.e., treatment success requires no additional glucose-raising interventions)

intercurrentEvents.name: Failure to achieve adequate insulin-induced hypoglycemia
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not achieve the required hypoglycemic nadir during the controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia procedure, resulting in non-evaluable primary outcome data

intercurrentEvents.name: Device or administration failure
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient experiences a device malfunction or incorrect administration of nasal glucagon or intramuscular glucagon by study site personnel, resulting in non-evaluable or missing primary outcome data

estimands.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Estimand
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with T1DM or T2DM who received at least one dose of study treatment (LY900018 or IMG) during the crossover study (Safety Population - all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment) Summary measure: Frequency and percentage of patients experiencing SAEs and TEAEs by system organ class and preferred term; descriptive statistics for vital signs; comparison between treatment groups.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation due to adverse event
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues study participation due to an adverse event prior to completion of the follow-up visit (26 to 30 days after last study treatment)

intercurrentEvents.name: Use of concomitant medications affecting safety assessments
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient uses concomitant medications during the study period that may confound the interpretation of adverse events or vital sign measurements

estimands.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with T1DM or T2DM who received at least one dose of study treatment and have evaluable pharmacokinetic samples (Pharmacokinetic (PK) Population - all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment with sufficient evaluable PK concentration-time data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (geometric mean, coefficient of variation) for AUC and Cmax; median and range for Tmax; geometric mean ratios with 90% confidence intervals for AUC and Cmax comparing LY900018 to IMG.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or non-evaluable PK samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing, hemolyzed, or otherwise non-evaluable pharmacokinetic blood samples that prevent derivation of one or more PK parameters

intercurrentEvents.name: Vomiting or nasal obstruction affecting drug absorption
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient experiences vomiting shortly after dosing or has nasal obstruction that may affect absorption and derived PK parameters

soaFootnotes.text: Samples for immunogenicity, should be collected every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline (ie, returns to within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer) or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment. biospecimenRetentions.description: A single blood sample for pharmacogenetic analysis is collected prior to or on Period 1 Day -1 and stored. The protocol indicates this sample is retained for pharmacogenetic analysis.

biospecimenRetentions.description: Immunogenicity samples are collected every 12 weeks (84±7 days) for treatment-emergent antidrug antibody (TE ADA) follow-up until the titer returns to baseline or up to 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

Although all AEs are recorded in the CRF after signing informed consent, SAE reporting to the sponsor begins after the patient has signed informed consent and has received investigational product. However, if an SAE occurs after signing informed consent, but prior to receiving investigational product, AND is considered reasonably possibly related to a study procedure then it MUST be reported.

Pregnancy (maternal or paternal exposure to investigational product) does not meet the definition of an AE. However, to fulfill regulatory requirements any pregnancy should be reported following the SAE process to collect data on the outcome for both mother and fetus.

Nonserious AEs obtained through the questionnaire are recorded and analyzed separately. Only SAEs elicited through the Nasal and Non-nasal Score Questionnaire and Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale are to be recorded as AEs via CRF and reported to Lilly or its designee within 24 hours as SAEs.

For the purposes of this study, an overdose of LY900018 or IMG is considered any dose that is higher than the assigned dose. Refer to the LY900018 IB and GlucaGen Summary of Product Characteristics for more information.

Blood pressure and pulse rate should be measured after at least 5 minutes supine. Unscheduled orthostatic vital signs should be assessed, if possible, during any AE of dizziness or posture-induced symptoms. If orthostatic measurements are required, patients should be supine for at least 5 minutes and stand for at least 2 minutes. If the patient feels unable to stand, supine vital signs only will be recorded.
Single ECGs will be collected and stored locally at the investigator's site. Triplicate ECGs will be electronically transmitted to a central ECG laboratory designated by Lilly.

The bedside PG level, measured using a glucose analyzer (Antsense Duo, HORIBA Ltd. or equivalent), must be 90 to 250 mg/dL to start the procedure. If the bedside PG is outside of this range, the hypoglycemia induction should be rescheduled.

If the target bedside PG level cannot be achieved within 4 hours after the start of insulin infusion, the hypoglycemia induction procedure will be terminated before glucagon administration, and the patient may have a carbohydrate-rich meal and be discharged from the CRU after medical assessment. studyInterventions.name: LY900018
studyInterventions.description: Nasal glucagon dry powder formulation (3 mg) for rescue treatment of insulin-induced hypoglycemia, administered intranasally by study site personnel using a single-use nasal dosing device

studyInterventions.name: GlucaGen (Intramuscular Glucagon)
studyInterventions.description: Intramuscular glucagon (1 mg) dry powder requiring reconstitution prior to IM injection, used as active comparator; manufactured by Novo Nordisk A/S

studyInterventions.name: Human regular insulin (IV infusion)
studyInterventions.description: Diluted human regular insulin (0.3 U/mL) administered by IV infusion to induce hypoglycemia during the study procedure; infusion rate starts at 2 mU/kg/min and may be adjusted up to 3 mU/kg/min (T1DM) or 4 mU/kg/min (T2DM)

studyInterventions.name: IV glucose
studyInterventions.description: Intravenous glucose administered if patient loses consciousness, PG declines too fast, or bedside PG remains <55 mg/dL at 30 minutes or <60 mg/dL at 45 minutes post glucagon dose

studyInterventions.name: Basal insulin analogs
studyInterventions.description: Permitted background therapy: insulin glargine (U-100 or U-300) or insulin degludec (U-100); last dose no later than 12 hours prior to hypoglycemia induction procedure

studyInterventions.name: Rapid-acting insulin analogs
studyInterventions.description: Permitted background therapy: insulin lispro, insulin aspart, or insulin glulisine; last prandial dose no later than 6 hours prior to hypoglycemia induction procedure

studyInterventions.name: Oral anti-hyperglycemic medications (OAMs)
studyInterventions.description: Permitted for T2DM patients: metformin, DPP-4 inhibitor, SGLT2 inhibitor, sulfonylurea (not more than half of maximum approved dose), glinides, alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, or thiazolidine (up to 3 OAMs); last dose no later than 12 hours prior to hypoglycemia induction procedure

studyInterventions.name: Acetaminophen (paracetamol)
studyInterventions.description: Permitted at investigator discretion for treatment of headaches; 1 g dose, maximum 2 g per 24 hours

studyInterventions.name: Anti-hypertensive medications
studyInterventions.description: Permitted if on stable regimen for at least 3 months at study entry; dose should remain unchanged throughout the study

studyInterventions.name: Anti-lipidemic medications
studyInterventions.description: Permitted if on stable regimen for at least 3 months at study entry; dose should remain unchanged throughout the study

studyInterventions.name: Beta-blockers
studyInterventions.description: Prohibited during the course of the study (daily systemic use)

studyInterventions.name: Indomethacin
studyInterventions.description: Prohibited during the course of the study

studyInterventions.name: Warfarin
studyInterventions.description: Prohibited during the course of the study

studyInterventions.name: Anticholinergic drugs
studyInterventions.description: Prohibited during the course of the study (daily systemic use)

studyInterventions.name: Pro-motility medications (e.g., metoclopramide, domperidone)
studyInterventions.description: Must be washed out at least 7 days before each treatment period and not taken while in the CRU; affect gastric motility

studyInterventions.name: Opiate medications (e.g., morphine)
studyInterventions.description: Must be washed out at least 7 days before each treatment period and not taken while in the CRU; affect gastric motility
